summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after developing worsening pain and drainage from a second-degree burn on her left lower leg sustained from spilled boiling pudding. Due to her wheelchair dependence and body habitus, she was unable to remove the hot liquid promptly. She was treated with unroofing of the burn by plastic surgery, daily Silvadene dressings, and antibiotics—IV Unasyn and oral linezolid—due to a vancomycin allergy. She remained afebrile with stable vitals. Her INR dropped to subtherapeutic levels, likely due to antibiotic interaction, prompting initiation of Lovenox bridging therapy, which successfully restored therapeutic anticoagulation. All chronic conditions, including HIV, hepatitis B and C, heart failure, asthma, and chronic pain, were managed with home medications. She improved clinically, completed necessary treatments, and was discharged home with services to continue antibiotics, wound care, and anticoagulation.
